You are implementing ONE requirement in the Apache Hadoop source tree at /workspace (a real upstream repo checked out at an earlier state).

REQUIREMENT SLUG: mapreduce-unused-imports
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/mapreduce-unused-imports.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/mapreduce-unused-imports.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: mapreduce-unused-imports" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/mapreduce-unused-imports.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/mapreduce-unused-imports.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.
  * IMPORTANT - a previous interrupted run left some UNCOMMITTED work in this tree. Before you start, run `cd /workspace && git status --short` and inspect `git diff` for the files you expect to touch. If part or all of this requirement is already implemented in the working tree but not yet committed, do NOT redo it from scratch: review it critically, finish/correct anything missing or wrong, then stage exactly those paths and commit as above. That uncommitted work is yours to claim when it belongs to this slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"mapreduce-unused-imports","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

import os, re, sys

def strip_comments(src):
    out = []; i = 0; n = len(src); state = 0
    while i < n:
        c = src[i]
        if state == 0:
            if c == '/' and i+1 < n and src[i+1] == '/': state = 1; i += 2; continue
            if c == '/' and i+1 < n and src[i+1] == '*': state = 2; i += 2; continue
            if c == '"': state = 3; out.append(' '); i += 1; continue
            if c == "'": state = 4; out.append(' '); i += 1; continue
            out.append(c); i += 1; continue
        elif state == 1:
            if c == '\n': state = 0; out.append('\n')
            i += 1; continue
        elif state == 2:
            if c == '*' and i+1 < n and src[i+1] == '/': state = 0; i += 2; out.append(' '); continue
            if c == '\n': out.append('\n')
            i += 1; continue
        elif state == 3:
            if c == '\\': i += 2; continue
            if c == '"': state = 0
            i += 1; continue
        elif state == 4:
            if c == '\\': i += 2; continue
            if c == "'": state = 0
            i += 1; continue
    return ''.join(out)

root = sys.argv[1]
dry = len(sys.argv) > 2 and sys.argv[2] == '--dry'
changed = []
for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
    if 'target' in dirpath.split(os.sep): continue
    for fn in sorted(filenames):
        if not fn.endswith('.java'): continue
        p = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
        src = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
        lines = src.split('\n')
        imp_idx = []
        body_lines = []
        for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
            m = re.match(r'^import\s+(static\s+)?([\w\.\*]+)\s*;', ln.strip())
            if m:
                imp_idx.append((i, m.group(2).split('.')[-1]))
            else:
                body_lines.append(ln)
        body = '\n'.join(body_lines)
        remove = set()
        for (i, simple) in imp_idx:
            if simple == '*': continue
            if not re.search(r'\b'+re.escape(simple)+r'\b', body):
                remove.add(i)
        if not remove: continue
        new = [ln for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if i not in remove]
        # collapse consecutive blank lines within the import region
        pkg = next((i for i, ln in enumerate(new) if ln.startswith('package ')), 0)
        lastimp = max((i for i, ln in enumerate(new) if re.match(r'^import\s', ln)), default=pkg)
        out = []
        for i, ln in enumerate(new):
            if pkg <= i <= lastimp and ln.strip() == '' and out and out[-1].strip() == '':
                continue
            out.append(ln)
        newsrc = '\n'.join(out)
        changed.append((p, len(remove)))
        if not dry:
            open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(newsrc)
for p, n in changed:
    print(n, p)
